rationale: The candidate is a coherent single object in all four views, so it passes basic cross-view consistency, but it is still too sealed and box-dominant for the neighborhood-living brief. The dominant gesture is a compact stepped/cantilevered block, yet the visible void is small and semantically weak; the ground edge does not read as a clearly public threshold toward the verified access side. The section does not convincingly articulate an active ground condition, court, or entry seam, and the stepped roof is more generic massing than an exceptional program-bearing terrace section. It resonates somewhat with the supplied references through low-rise courtyard/terrace logic, but it under-delivers those spatial principles. Program fit therefore fails the hard gate because the mass does not sufficiently support an active neighborhood edge plus legible public void/terrace relationship.
